title: ASK DON’T TELL: REDUCING SYCOPHANCY IN LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS

bias_targets.methodology: The paper measures sycophancy (a form of response bias where models favor user-affirming responses) by using controlled, content-matched prompts that vary input framing (questions vs. non-questions, epistemic certainty, and perspective). It evaluates model outputs using a rubric-based LLM-as-a-judge approach that scores excessive agreement, flattery, avoiding disagreement, user preference alignment, and validation seeking.
